zbpop3-p01.summary: Ostermann's evasive answer about the Russian regiments stationed in Poland kept Deboli from asking formally; he sees that Russia is not disposed to withdraw them and will press again at the next conference, arguing that the Emperor, travelling to Kiev, will see them with his own eyes.

zbpop3-p04.summary: Deboli expects an answer tomorrow on the King's letter about the regiment. Joseph II will come to Kherson rather than Kiev; Potemkin will receive the Empress at Krichev and Kiev; the affair of the Princess of Württemberg troubles the grand-ducal couple.

zbpop3-p07.summary: A talk with Ostermann, who refuses the withdrawal of the Russian regiment and blames Deboli's vehemence. Deboli thinks everything depends on Potemkin, fears the Commission he wants, and suggests the King write to him before Kiev; then the affair of the Palatine of Ruthenia and a castellan's son come without leave or passport.

zbpop3-p13.summary: Foreign ministers await an audience; the Empress received three of them at Tsarskoye Selo in very good humour. Hetman Branicki and his wife are to come to St Petersburg this winter, and there are hopes he will regain the King's favour.

zbpop3-p15.summary: Three posts came with no letter. The answer to the King's letter will come from the Empress herself. The British envoy has left; Ségur's tragedy 'Coriolan' was staged at the Hermitage; Ségur leaves within a week with the Prince de Ligne.

zbpop3-p21.summary: Deboli asks how the King's letter and its allegorical idea were received. The Empress came back to town, attended the Preobrazhensky regiment's feast at the Summer Palace and moved into the Winter Palace.

zbpop3-p23.summary: A courier to Warsaw; Cobenzl and the Austrian courier; the Turks have declared war; French mediation; Ostermann on France and Berlin; Prussian recruitment; the Prince de Ligne wishes to write to the King.

zbpop3-p28.summary: Back from Gatchina. Cobenzl says the alliance binds the Emperor to war; the Council debates peace with the Turks; Ligne's letter goes with the Austrian courier and he asks about an extraordinary Sejm.

zbpop3-p30.summary: Wielhorski has arrived on business of the castellan's wife Ogińska (probable) and Deboli has introduced him. Starosta Potocki would have lost 200,000 roubles in merchants' failures had they not been withdrawn, and still loses through the exchange rate.

zbpop3-p33.summary: Before tomorrow's conference: Rumyantsev's division has entered Turkish territory to screen Poland; Deboli will ask when to expect the answer on the alliance project. His three conclusions: Russia wants a short war (take Ochakov, then peace), the Emperor will do little at first, and a Franco-Russian union is hard.

zbpop3-p37.summary: A long talk with Markov: Russia still wants to shield Poland in this war and come to an agreement, but will not guarantee a territory for Poland; the aim should be keeping, not enlarging, the country. Deboli answers that Russian inaction would be read as abandonment. The rest of the piece is in other tables and not read.

zbpop3-g1.summary: Gołuchowski has nothing to add on the Empress's journey. He denies the report about Prince Repnin; Buchholtz is said to have announced the entry of 10 Russian regiments, causing alarm in Warsaw.

zbpop3-g3.summary: At court the foreign ministers pressed him about the 10 regiments said to be entering Poland; he answered he had nothing certain. The Danish minister asked about Şahin Giray; he said he knew no more than the Hamburg papers.

zbpop3-g4.summary: Asked to find out Grand Duke Paul's taste in saddle horses to be sent from Poland, Gołuchowski reports the riding master's requirements: calm, unafraid of firing and cannon, lively, sound and strong; he doubts one horse can have all these qualities and that it can arrive in time.

system: One-part Polish code in shuffled letter blocks (key ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska', 8 Mar 1783): groups 1-1969 for letters, syllables, endings, words and names, signal group 2345, nulls from 1970; half-marked groups (136 1/2 = Nas).
